prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK Manifesto 2024 (max 500 words)

Core pledges:
- Freeze non-essential immigration; new measures to end illegal Channel crossings.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while remaining free at point of use; tackle staffing shortages.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; increase higher-rate threshold to £70,000.
- Reduce energy bills by scrapping levies/Net Zero policies; expand domestic oil and gas.
- Cut government waste to fund services and tax reductions.

Immigration:
- Freeze non-essential immigration; create a Department of Immigration.
- Detain and deport illegal arrivals; process claims offshore; bar asylum from safe-country arrivals; no legal aid for non-citizens.
- Return small boat crossings to France; leave the ECHR if required.
- Deport foreign criminals after sentences; withdraw citizenship for serious offenders.
- Bar student dependents; restrict post-study stays to essential skills; close abuse of routes.
- Five-year residency/employment for benefits.
- Employer immigration tax: raise NI to 20% for foreign workers (exempt health/care and firms ≤5 staff).
- Estimated savings: £5–10bn pa; employer tax ~£4bn pa.

Government spending and waste:
- Stop paying interest on QE reserves to commercial banks (~£35bn pa).
- Save 5% across departments without affecting front line (~£50bn pa).
- Cut foreign aid by 50% (~£6bn pa); improve HMRC collection; deregulate retained EU law.
- Potential savings claimed: ~£91bn pa.

Economy – personal:
- Lift income tax start to £20k; cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy; scrap green levies.
- Stamp Duty: 0% up to £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% above.
- Reinstate VAT-free tourist shopping; reform IHT (0% under £2m; 20% above with charity option).
- Cost: ~£70bn pa.

Economy – business:
- No corporation tax for profits ≤£100k; main rate to 20% then 15% (year 3).
- Abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals.
- Planning and regulatory simplification; easier hiring/firing; major tax code simplification.
- Cost: ~£18bn pa.

NHS:
- Zero basic-rate tax for NHS/social care staff for 3 years; lift training caps; student fee write-offs tied to service.
- Use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private health/insurance.
- Voucher guarantees for GP (3 days), consultant (3 weeks), operations (9 weeks).
- Efficiency/management reforms; A&E demand management; public inquiry into excess deaths.
- Cost: ~£17bn pa.

Energy/Net Zero:
- Scrap Net Zero targets and renewable subsidies; fast-track North Sea and shale; expand nuclear (SMRs) and other tech.
- Claimed public sector savings: ~£30bn pa.

Law and order/justice:
- Recruit 40,000 police; expand stop-and-search; tougher sentencing; reduce DE&I roles; more visible policing.
- Justice budget to £12bn; mandatory life for violent repeat offenders; build 10,000 detention places; adjust hate crime definitions.
- Costs: policing ~£3bn pa; justice ~£2bn pa.

Other policies (highlights):
- Education: curriculum changes; restrictions on gender identity policies in schools; 20% tax relief on independent schooling; loan interest scrapped; expand PRUs. Cost ~£5bn pa.
- Benefits: stricter conditionality and assessments; savings ~£15bn pa.
- Defence: spending to 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay uplift; veterans’ department. Cost ~£14bn pa.
- Housing: planning reform, prioritisation in social housing; landlord tax changes; leaseholder protections. Cost neutral.
- Transport: scrap remaining HS2 (save £25bn one-off); end ULEZ/LTNs; utility ownership reform; £5bn pa savings over 5 years.
- Agriculture: budget to £3bn; shift subsidies; reduce red tape. Cost ~£2bn pa.
- Fisheries: tighter control of UK waters; rebuild processing. Cost ~£2bn pa.
- Constitutional/culture: ECHR exit; Lords/civil service/postal voting reforms; PR referendum; BBC licence abolition; free speech bill. Largely cost neutral.

Funding summary:
- Claimed annual savings: ~£150bn plus £10bn from growth assumptions = £160bn pa.
- Claimed annual costs: ~£141bn pa.
